MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 27, 2024
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Kelley at 5:03 p.m., on February 27, 2024, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on February 22, 2024, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Goodell ~ arrived 5:04pm
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 and 54957.6. The Parties to the
  Negotiations Are the City and City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiator
  is Dennis Wilberg.

CS2. Liability Claims and Existing Litigation: Claimants: Villanea GAL Castillo, Loos-
  Hannifan, Heirs of Cade Veen, Pavlisin, and Kronich Gath & OC Generations V
  Limited Partnership: Agency Claimed Against - City of Mission Viejo and: Significant
  Exposure to Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph (2) of Subdivision (d) Section 54956.9 (5
  cases)
City Council Minutes  1  February 27, 2024
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:04 pm Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:07 pm with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley announced that there were two Close Session items, labor negotiations and
liability claims and litigation. The City Council was updated but no reportable actions occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Kelley

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize City Manager Dennis Wilberg for Receiving the Prestigious Wes McClure
  Award from the League of California Cities

  Mayor Kelley presented a certificate of commendation to City Manager Dennis Wilberg.

P2. Recognize the Trabuco Hills High School Thundering Mustangs Marching Unit for
  Winning the California State Western Band Association Grand Championship for
  Class 1A-3A

  Mayor Kelley presented certificates of commendation.

P3. Orange County Vector Control Presentation on the Sterile Insect Technique (SIT)
  Project

  Received presentation from Orange County Vector Control Director of Scientific Technical
  Services Amber Semrow.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Bob Breton, M.V.: Congratulated City Manager Dennis Wilberg on receiving the Wes McClure
Award from the League of California Cities. He highlighted the many achievements Dennis has
contributed to the City.

Jesse Matlock, M.V.: Introduced himself as President of Mission Viejo Girls Softball League.
He thanked the City Council and Staff for all their support.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Thanked Attorney’s Aaron Hand, Lee Fink, Brett Murdoch, and Michael
Schlesinger for all their work in protecting the voters in Mission Viejo. She stated that the Court
of Appeals ruling will be published which will be a permanent record for future elections. Lastly,

City Council Minutes  2  February 27, 2024
 she invited residents to an Orange County First Event at the Norman P. Murray Center on
February 29 to learn about the security of Orange County Elections.

Tom Moore, M.V.: Spoke on the Coe Area Vision Plan and voiced support for the development
on a specific plan for this intersection. He outlined his suggestions for this project.

Jerry Bryant, MV: Congratulated the City Manager on his award. Spoke on the City to use local
pest control companies for the mosquito problems and suggested Mosquito Authority.

CONSENT CALENDAR

City Manager Dennis Wilberg announced that Item 13 for the Purchase of (1) 2024 Chevrolet
Colorado will be considered at a future Council Meeting.

Items 6, 12, and 14 were removed by Council Member Vasquez from the Consent Calendar for
separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of February 13, 2024, as
  presented.

2.  General Check Register Dated February 2, 2024 in the Amount of $2,909,660.94

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  General Check Register Dated February 9, 2024 in the Amount of $3,380,805.84

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Golf Check Register Dated February 2, 2024 in the Amount of $20,782.17

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

City Council Minutes  3  February 27, 2024
 5.  Golf Check Register Dated February 9, 2024 in the Amount of $254,214.37

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

7.  Amending the City of Mission Viejo Salary Schedule

  Adopted Resolution 24-05 Amending the City's Salary Schedule Effective January 1, 2024.

8.  Agreement for Document Scanning Services.

  Authorized the City Manager to Execute an Agreement with Matrix Imaging Products, Inc.
  (A24-06) for Document Scanning Services.

9.  Annual Park and Facility Hardscape Construction Improvement Contract

  Approved the 14th Amendment to the existing maintenance contract with S. Parker
  Engineering, Inc., in an amount not to exceed $165,000.00.

10. Security Guard Services - Civic Core Area Facility

  Approved the First Amendment with The Green Angels Private Security in the amount not
  to exceed $25,000.00.

11. Security Guard Services - Special Events

  Approved the First Amendment with The Green Angels Private Security in the amount not
  to exceed $25,000.00.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

6.  Lower Curtis Park Biological Monitoring and Reporting

  Council Member Vasquez asked when the pad will be complete and if the City might
  consider using that land as a temporary parking for commercial vehicles to free up
  neighborhood streets.

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon stated that the pad will be completed in roughly 1
  to 2 years and after that it will be up to the City Council to decide on the usage of this pad.

  Motion made by Council Member Vasquez, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  authorize the issuance of a purchase order in the amount of $41,190 to Glenn Lukos
  Associates, Inc. for biological monitoring and reporting for Lower Curtis Park.

City Council Minutes  4  February 27, 2024
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

12. Lease Agreement for Two (2) Public Services Replacement Vehicles

  Council Member Vasquez asked if there were any options for EV or Hybrid trucks and if any
  other cities have switched here whole fleet from gas to electric or hybrid.

  Director of Public Services explained that at this time there are no electric three-quarter ton
  pick trucks. He did indicate that all of the City’s pool cars are electric Chevy Volts, as well
  as our Code Enforcement vehicles are Toyota Priuses. He stated he is not familiar with other
  cities completely converted to electric or hybrid.

  Council Member Bucknum advocated for a diversified fleet due to the challenges California
  is facing with electric reliability.

  Motion made by Council Member Vasquez, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to
  authorize the City Manager to enter into a Lease Agreement with Enterprise Fleet
  Management (EFM) (A24-07) for the lease of two (2) 2024 Chevrolet Silverado
  Replacement Vehicles.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

14. CIP 23338 - Event Structure in the GARDEN+GRILLE at the OSO CREEK GOLF
  COURSE

  Council Members asked various questions and Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay
  explained the purchase of the structure and the benefits it will have for events.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to (1)
  Award a contract and issued a purchase order to Shelter Structures America (A24-08) for the
  event structure in the GARDEN+GRILLE at the Oso Creek Golf Course (CIP 23338) in an
  amount not to exceed $187,930.70; and (2) adopt Resolution 24-06 Amending the Oso Creek
  Golf Course Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Operating Budget to transfer funds to CIP 23338 for the
  purchase of an event structure at the GARDEN+GRILLE.

City Council Minutes  5  February 27, 2024
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

15. 2024 USA Triathlon National Championships in Mission Viejo

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch asked that on the registration form participants indicate where they
  are staying so that we can show our neighboring cities that they are financially benefiting
  from this race in regards to TOT take at their hotels.

  Council Member Vasquez asked for clarification on why the City of Lake Forest denied
  funds for this event and voiced concerns that the City say yes to a lot of outside organizations.

  Council Member Goodell stated that he did reach out to a Lake Forest Council Member and
  was told that it was very difficult to quantify if their city financially benefits from our event
  so this will be a good way to track where the participants are staying.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Voiced her concerns on Empower Multi-Sports and that the event is
  being sponsored by Game Day CBD. She asked that the Council reject this item.

  Council Member Bucknum asked if there was any data from the Nadadores that Lake Forest
  has benefited from their Meets and suggested that we give that analysis to the Lake Forest.
  She asked that the Chamber of Commerce give information for the goody bags that lists local
  restaurants or some sort of a coupon book for our businesses in Mission Viejo. She stated
  that this is an economic benefit for our businesses in our City and that is why we have focused
  on the sports economy. She indicated that she would be willing to give less than $20,000.

  Mayor Kelley feels this will be a national event with news coverage and agrees with the
  $20,000.

  Council Member Vasquez stated she understands the economic benefits but questions giving
  them more money and that we need to think more about this.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to
  approve an additional in-kind $10,000 to be matched by private sponsorship.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum and Ruesch
  NOES:  Goodell, Kelley, and Vasquez.
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  6  February 27, 2024
   Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to approve an
  additional in-kind up to $20,000 to be matched by private sponsorship, require that the
  athletes include on their registration form what City they will be staying in so we can track
  what other cities are benefiting from this event, and that the Chamber of Commerce provide
  an insert in the participants goody bag with coupons for local restaurants and business within
  the City.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Ruesch
  NOES:  Vasquez
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

16. Desktop and Laptop Computer Replacement

  Director of Information Technology David Meyer and Director of Administrative Services
  gave the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 24-07 Authorizing Execution of Property Schedule No. 2 and Related
  Documents Under an Existing Master Tax-Exempt Lease-Purchase Agreement with U.S.
  Bancorp Government Leasing and Finance, Inc. (A24-09); and (2) authorize City staff to
  execute a purchase order with Dell in the amount of $457,968.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

17. Modifications to the City of Mission Viejo Purchasing Policy and Procedure Manual

  Administrative Services Manager Susan Knudson gave the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  adopt Resolution 24-08 Adopting the City's Purchasing Policy and Procedure Manual
  Effective February 27, 2024.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  7  February 27, 2024
 18. Cost Recovery Policy Review and Update

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas gave the staff report.

  Council Member Bucknum asked that when this item comes back to have a breakdown of
  membership fees for resident vs. non-resident and youth in regards to tennis memberships.

  Council Member Vasquez asked for a breakdown of residents vs. non-residents for all the
  facilities.

  Director Dyas indicated that this will probably come back to the Council the second meeting
  of April.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 24-09 Amending Council Policy No. 0300-11 - Cost Recovery Policies.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

19. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Received report from Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch.

CITY MANAGER REPORTS

20. Climate Change Mitigation

  Ed Maurer, M.V.: Thanked the City Council for having this on the agenda and asked that
  they remember to look at this report through the eyes of young people as they will be around
  at the end of the century and will be living through climate change.

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister gave the presentation.

  By consensus the City Council received the presentation.

City Manager Dennis Wilberg announced that City is in the process of updating its Local Hazard
Mitigation Plan and is in the public comment period. The City received grant funding from FEMA
to complete the update. A draft plan has been completed and has been posted on the City’s
webpage. Hard copies are also located at City Hall and the NPM Center for the public to view.
The public comment period concludes March 6th. Once comments are received, the plan will be
submitted to Cal OES, FEMA and the City Council for review and approval. Secondly, he
announced that Captain Chris McDonald will be leaving us in April. He has been asked to head
City Council Minutes  8  February 27, 2024
 up the newly created Real-Time Prevention Center in Tustin. The City will begin the process to
replace him.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

21. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum attended the Love Fest themed Night Market and had a wonderful
time. She held another California Sober Living & Recovery Home Task Meeting that is getting a
lot of attention. They are looking at receiving contributions from each of the member cities and
the Association of California Cities is going to house that tracking of those dollars under their
organization once their board approves it. She stated that Council Member Ruesch is on that board.
Council Member Bucknum said they are looking for a solution for Mission Viejo to not be paying
for it going forward because the County is going to have one of the Board of Supervisors,
potentially Katrina Foley and John Wagner to join as one of our co-chairs. The County is taking a
bigger role in this and there is legislation that is being introduced and we are making some progress
and she plans to have a presentation at an upcoming meeting. She attended the Oso Fit 5k Fun Run
and cheered on Council Member Vasquez. She stated that she appreciated the presentation earlier
and how we recognize our youth. She thanked speaker Jess Matlock for thanking the Council for
investing in the youth. Council Member Bucknum stated she is proud to be a part of a City that
makes decisions that align with that investment. She reminisced back when her family hosted a
swimmer from Mexico named Juan Rodella back in the nineties for two years and talked about
how he became part of their family and recently came back and visited them. She encouraged
residents to consider housing a student athlete from another country, it’s an amazing experience.
She announced that their will be a Women’s Business Conference on Friday March 22 at the
Laguna Hills Community Center and all the local assembly women will be hosting and she will be
a moderator. Lastly, she stated that they will be announcing her as the Women of the Year for the
71st Assembly District by Assemblywoman Kate Sanchez. She invited her female colleagues and
staff to attend.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell announced that he recently moved to Casa del Sol. He highlighted the
recent visits the Sports Tourism Committee had from Germany and indicated that the Netherlands
will be visiting in the coming weeks. Both Germany and Netherlands are interested in bringing
their whole Olympic teams for the 2028 Olympics as a staging area and training area prior to the
games. He stated it’s an exciting opportunity and that the efforts of the committee are paying off.
Council Member Goodell also mentioned that Mexico’s football group also toured our facilities
for training ground for their soccer teams. He stated he is very excited about some of things that
are happening across the street and that the project is moving forward and the new event space at

City Council Minutes  9  February 27, 2024
 the golf course. Lastly, he mentioned that information on the parking garage for the Oso Creek
project will be coming back at an upcoming meeting next month.

Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez attended the OCFA Truck 9 Pushing Ceremony with several of her
colleagues and had a fun time. She participate in the Oso Fit 5k. She stated that girl scout cookie
season is wrapping but there is still time to purchase cookies.

Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch

Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch highlighted the city-wide Dump Day Event on February 17. He stated the
u-hauls were filled by 10 am and it was great to be able to help our residents along with e-waste
for residents to get rid of electronic equipment. Mayor Pro Tem commented on the Aquarium of
Pacific mobile aquarium program that was being held the same day by the library. Lastly, he
attended the subterranean soundscapes concert featuring WestBeat Acapella which was an
amazing event and the sound was incredible. He praised staff for setting up theses tunnel events.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley attended a ribbon cutting ceremony for Mariners Church that opened in the
Kaleidoscope where the old Islands restaurant used to be and wished them success at this new
location. She also attended the tour with Germany visit and it was great to be able to show off our
City. Mayor Kelley attended the first meeting of the Police Services Citizens Academy to greet
the participants and was very impressed with the number of attendees. She also attended the OCFA
Truck Push event as well the opening ceremony for Viejo Little League, and Oso Fit 5k. Lastly,
she again congratulated City Manager Wilberg for his award from the League of California Cities
and congratulated Council Member Bucknum on being named Woman of the Year for the 71st
Assembly District.

ADJOURNMENT AT 9:56 PM TO TUESDAY, March 12, 2024, AT 5:00 P.M.

______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of March 12, 2024

City Council Minutes  10  February 27, 2024
